title: Seventh stale-suite triage draw: 84 untriaged unrun test files across ten directories, each executed on its own, and the five directories that came back clean wired into CI

scope.drawnFrom: governedRiskRanking from scripts/quality/test-ci-coverage-census.mjs, ranks 8 and 10-18, re-derived on this base rather than read from the committed snapshot
scope.whyRank9IsAbsent: Rank 9 (src/__tests__/integration/ops, 14 untriaged files) is deliberately not drawn: T-033 and T-074 each already own named files inside it, so it is not a clean directory draw and needs those two settled first. That exclusion is the filing's, carried forward here unchanged.
scope.censusDriftAtThisBase: The committed census artifact matches a fresh run on this base, so the draw is reproducible from the census rather than asserted. Ranks 8 and 10-18 reproduce exactly: 23 + 10 + 8 + 7 + 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 84, every row band unclassified, score 0, admittedBy untriaged_unrun_work.
scope.disjointnessIsAsserted: src/__tests__/behaviors/t492-stale-suite-triage-record.test.ts reads every sibling record and fails if any path appears in two. The filing names five prior records to reconcile against; this reconciles against all seven stale-suite records plus the two non-stale triage records (t478, t758) by exact path, and 0 of the 84 appeared in any of them.

jestEvidence.how: Each of the 84 was executed on its own with `npx jest --runTestsByPath <path> --no-coverage --ci --json --outputFile`, and every count in suites[] is read out of that run's JSON by script rather than typed. --runTestsByPath for all 84 so that no path is read as a regex.
jestEvidence.executedAt: 2026-09-27T08:13:21Z onward, before any verdict in this record was written
jestEvidence.harnessFoundTests: Asserted rather than assumed: all 84 runs report numTotalTestSuites 1, exactly one entry in testResults, and numTotalTests greater than zero. A run that matched no file reports zero and exits green, which is the failure mode this check exists for. 0 of 84 anomalies.

caseAttribution.method: A case is byte-matching when its body references an identifier bound to the text of a file read off disk -- a const, a derived view of one, or a helper function that returns one. Mechanical, so no judgement of mine decides it.
caseAttribution.reliableWhen: Static `it(`/`test(` openers equal the runtime case count. A suite whose cases are generated in a loop or by `.each` has more runtime cases than openers, and then per-case attribution has no denominator.
caseAttribution.whyPublishedRatherThanGuessed: 22 of the 84 cannot be attributed case by case. Publishing a share for them would be inventing a number, and the suite-level answer -- does this suite read repository file text at all -- is reliable for all 84 and is the one the scanner rule turns on. So the instrument's limit is published instead of hidden, and the guard asserts the suite-level and case-level fields stay consistent with it.

scannerClassification.rule: sourceTextScanner is declared per row and constrained two ways. It may never be true for a suite the mechanical classifier found reads no file text. Where it is false and the classifier found the suite DOES read file text, the row must carry either partialSourceTextCases above zero or a written notAScannerReason -- so every departure from the mechanical signal carries a reason a reviewer can weigh.
scannerClassification.inheritedRules: T-550's rule and T-556's narrowing, kept in full: a source-text scanner is never wired into CI, and one whose subject genuinely IS the text says so in writing and is still not wired.

wiring.namedAsDirectories: Each of the five is named as a DIRECTORY, not file by file, for the reason the workflow's own header gives: file-by-file wiring is the shape of the defect, and a suite added to one of these directories tomorrow runs the day it lands.
wiring.provenBy: src/__tests__/behaviors/t492-wired-directory-ci-coverage.test.ts, which answers through the census's own resolver rather than by grepping the workflow for a string, and which also refuses a re-add to the dark baseline.
wiring.fiveOfTenOnly: Five of the ten drawn directories are wired. The other five each hold at least one row this record hands to another item -- a red suite, or a source-text scanner the inherited rule refuses to wire -- and a directory is wired by fixing it, never by adding it to a green command.

heldDirectories.src/__tests__/hygiene: 3 of 6 red, 5 of 6 source-text scanners. 2 green rows wait on T-494.
heldDirectories.src/__tests__/integration/agents: 2 of 8 red, 8 of 8 read component text. 2 green rows with a text-scanning appendix wait on T-494.
heldDirectories.src/lib/integrations/ai-egress/__tests__: 0 red. Held by ONE row: a migration-text scanner the inherited rule refuses to wire. 5 green behavioural suites are dark for one file's sake, which is the most expensive single row in this draw.
heldDirectories.src/lib/intelligence/ask/__tests__: 3 of 23 red, 4 of 23 scanners. 18 green behavioural rows wait on T-494 -- the largest block of ready work this draw found.
heldDirectories.src/lib/intelligence/canonical: 2 of 6 red, both red since the commit that created them. 3 green rows wait on T-494. Not a __tests__ directory, so a __tests__-shaped glob would miss it entirely.

drawConcentration.whyItMatters: Rank 8 alone holds 23 of the 84 -- more than twice the entire pool the first six draws could see between them, which is the measurement T-475 asked for. A reader told 'ten directories, highest governed risk first' pictures an even spread; the top directory is 27% of the draw and the bottom five are 6 files each. The concentration is derived here from the rows rather than narrated, so a record edited after the fact cannot understate it.

vacuousControlsDeclared.sourceTextScanner: NOT VACUOUS. 19 of the 84 read repository file text and 15 carry sourceTextScanner true; the control refusing to wire any of those fired 15 times, and 0 of the 35 rows this item actually wires reads file text at all. That last number is the one that matters: the rule did not merely pass, it separated the draw. The 4 rows that read text and are NOT called scanners each carry a written reason or a named set of byte-matching cases, which is the second half of the same control.
vacuousControlsDeclared.redSuites: NOT VACUOUS. 10 of the 84 are red -- 39 failing cases -- and every one carries a verdict that does not assume it passes. Two of them, in src/lib/intelligence/canonical, have been red since the single commit that created both the suite and the module it tests, four months ago, which no workflow could report because no workflow ran them.
vacuousControlsDeclared.partialSourceTextCases: NOT VACUOUS. 3 rows carry partialSourceTextCases above zero (8, 9, 15 cases), so the control naming every byte-matching case inside a non-scanner suite fired rather than passing over an empty set.
vacuousControlsDeclared.caseAttribution: NOT VACUOUS in the direction that matters: 22 of the 84 cannot be attributed case by case and the record says which, so the guard is asserting a published limit rather than an empty one.

forbiddenEdits: No file this record passes judgement on was edited. No failing case was weakened, skipped, quarantined or deleted to reach a green run; the 10 red suites are still red on this base and are handed on with their diagnoses.

There is no runtime observable, because the retired path still resolves -- an import from it works perfectly at run time, which is exactly why it drifts back. The text of the import statement is the artifact under test, so this is not a byte assertion standing in for behaviour.
suites.rationale: RED, and it found something real rather than having gone stale. src/app/api/intelligence/ask/route.ts:13 and :14 import from @/lib/agents/sentinel-reasoning while the canonical path is @/lib/agent/; src/lib/agents/ still exists on disk holding that one module. The mechanical classifier agrees -- it found no binding to any file's text at all.
suites.rationale: Green, 1 case, 0 failing. A duplicate route file is a Next.js build-time ambiguity, and this is the only thing in the tree that asks. Held with its directory for T-494 because three of its six siblings are red.

suites.rationale: RED, and stale rather than right. It asserts MaestroChrome.tsx contains the eight bytes "'/home'" in single quotes; the file carries "/home" in double quotes at line 12. A quote-style reformat broke it. The invariant it is reaching for -- NexusTopNav is mounted once, by the chrome, and not again by the nested Learn layout -- is observable by rendering the layout, so the repair is a render assertion and not a better regular expression.

movedTo.reason: Rewritten from a source-text scanner into a rendering suite and moved beside the component it drives; the new contents contain JSX and require the .tsx extension. It is NOT placed in src/__tests__/behaviors, because that directory's coverage floor thresholds an aggregate across every file its suites touch and passes with under a point of headroom, so a suite importing a component tree fails it with every case green. The verdict, counts and execution numbers recorded above describe the file as drawn at the base commit and are unchanged. Record: docs/architecture/t495-learn-shell-chrome-triage.json.

suites.textIsTheSubjectReason: The subject is a prohibition on a literal appearing anywhere in the source of a shipped surface. A literal that is never rendered on any path still leaks the moment someone reads the bundle, so there is no run of the product that can answer the question the suite asks; only the bytes can. It scans through a scan() helper rather than a bound constant, which is why the case-level classifier attributes none of its cases and the suite-level signal is the one to trust.
suites.rationale: Green, 1 case, 0 failing, and it is a governance control rather than a unit test: it walks the surface tree and refuses a named literal. It cannot be wired while it lives in a directory with three red siblings, and the honest long-term home for it is the repo's own lint/governance lane rather than a jest suite, which is what T-495 has to decide.

suites.textIsTheSubjectReason: Its subject is a committed migration's text, and what it asserts is the ABSENCE of statements -- no INSERT INTO, no UPDATE of a pattern table, no DELETE FROM, no TRUNCATE, no DROP TABLE, no ALTER TABLE outside the one table it owns. An absence in a migration cannot be observed by running the migration; a run that destroys data looks exactly like a run that does not until you check what is gone. Only the file can answer, so this is not a byte assertion standing in for behaviour.
